No external models or textures.
2. Lighting: physically plausible shading (diffuse + specular, gamma-correct output) with a key light and soft fill/ambient light; metal finishes must read as metal.
3. A <canvas> fills the main viewing area.

Configurator UI (beside the canvas on desktop, below it on mobile)
4. Product name "Halo Desk Lamp", the price "$289", a one-sentence description and an "Add to cart" button.
5. Three finish swatches — buttons with class="swatch" named "Matte Black", "Brushed Brass" and "Glacier White" (visible text or aria-label) — that change the lamp's material with a smooth ~400 ms transition. The selected swatch has aria-pressed="true" and its name is shown in an element with id="finish-name".
6. A button id="lamp-toggle" (aria-pressed) switches the lamp on: the bulb glows and a warm light from the shade visibly lights the floor and the lamp itself.
7. A button id="autorotate" (aria-pressed) toggles a slow auto-rotation that is on by default, pauses while the user drags and resumes 3 s after the last interaction.

Controls
8. Orbit by dragging (mouse and touch), zoom with the wheel and pinch, with smooth damping; pitch and zoom are clamped so the camera never goes below the floor or inside the lamp; double-click resets the view; arrow keys rotate when the canvas has focus.

1. At least 100,000 star particles rendered with a single draw call (gl.POINTS or THREE.Points) using additive blending and round, soft point sprites whose size attenuates with distance.
2. Structure: a bright, warm central bulge and N spiral arms (N = 2–6, chosen with <input type="range" id="arms">, default 4) with stars concentrated along the arms; colours shift from warm yellow-white in the core to blue-white in the arms, with a sprinkle of pink star-forming regions. Add a faint background star field.
3. Motion: differential rotation — inner stars orbit faster than outer ones — computed on the GPU in the vertex shader from a time uniform (do not rewrite a 100k-element buffer from JavaScript every frame). The arms must stay recognisable over time instead of winding up into a featureless disc (for example a density-wave approach: slightly elliptical or lobed orbits whose orientation changes with radius). An <input type="range" id="speed"> scales time.
4. A button id="supernova" triggers a shockwave: a bright ring expanding from the core over about 2 s that pushes and brightens the stars it passes.
5. Camera: drag to orbit (mouse and touch), wheel/pinch zoom within limits, and a very slow automatic drift when idle.
6. HUD: the total number of stars in an element id="count" (formatted like 120,000) and the current frame rate in an element id="fps".
7. Adaptive quality: when the frame rate drops, lower the render resolution and/or draw only a random subset of the stars — but keep at least 100,000 in the buffer.

1. Standard colour scheme: white on top (U), yellow on the bottom (D), green front (F), blue back (B), red right (R), orange left (L). A black body with slightly rounded stickers and small gaps between the pieces.
2. Face turns with the keys U, D, L, R, F and B — clockwise as seen when looking straight at that face — and Shift + key for counter-clockwise. The model must stay mathematically correct: for example (R U R′ U′) repeated 6 times returns the cube to solved.
3. On-screen buttons for all 12 turns (U, U′, D, D′, L, L′, R, R′, F, F′, B, B′) inside a container with id="move-pad" — required for touch screens, each with an accessible name.
4. A button id="scramble" applies 25 random turns (never the same face twice in a row) quickly; a button id="reset" restores the solved cube.
5. An element id="moves" shows the number of turns since the last scramble/reset; an element id="timer" shows the solve time (m:ss.s), starting with the first turn after a scramble and stopping when the cube is solved.
6. When a turn leaves the cube solved, show a "Solved!" overlay with the move count and time.
7. Drag on the canvas to orbit the camera around the cube (mouse and touch). The default view shows the U, F and R faces.

Controls
- Drag to orbit (mouse and touch), wheel/pinch zoom within limits.
- A <select id="quality"> with "High" and "Low" options (e.g. step count and shadow quality).
